summary: Privileged SSH session observed after employee clicked external LinkedIn message — possible credential replay
description: Issue summary: A privileged SSH session tied to a service jump host (jmp-priv-us-east) was observed minutes after an employee clicked a suspicious LinkedIn message. Impact: potential lateral access to infra and short-lived use of a service account token. Environment: production (us-east-1) main cluster and jump hosts. Initial detection: automated login anomaly alert from Bastion monitor at 09:12 UTC showing an unexpected IP (45.76.22.198) and an interactive SSH session under user 's.opera' followed by immediate sudo activity.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Employee received an external LinkedIn direct message with a shortened URL. 2) Employee clicked link and completed what appeared to be an OAuth consent page that requested GitHub and LinkedIn public profile access. 3) Within 6 minutes, Bastion Audit logged a new SSH session from a foreign IP and MFA prompt activity. 4) Session escalated to a privileged shell via su/sudo and pulled a short-lived service token using an internal helper script.
observed_evidence:
- Bastion logs (bastion-prod-2026-03-13-09.log) show SSH from 45.76.22.198 -> port 22 -> user s.opera.
- MFA push logged but employee reported they did not approve (push_id=push-9a34).
- Internal helper script /opt/tools/token-fetcher wrote token to /tmp/tmpX3 and executed curl to metrics.redwood-internal.svc:443.
- Cloud IAM logs show STS AssumeRole for role 'infra-maintainer' with session name 's-opera-20260313-0918' from IP 45.76.22.198.
- GitHub OAuth grant recorded at 09:07 UTC for app 'ExternalCollab' with scopes: repo, read:user (employee reports consenting to 'basic profile' only).
iocs: IPs: [45.76.22.198], User-Agent strings: 'curl/7.79.1', OAuth client_id: 3f2a-extern-cc, Bastion session id: bast-94321, temporary token id: tk-02b4
immediate_actions_taken:
- Rotated credentials for service account referenced in token logs.
- Forced password reset for user 's.opera' and invalidated active sessions (bastion + console).
- Blocked IP 45.76.22.198 at perimeter and added to firewall denylist.
- Revoked the OAuth token for app 'ExternalCollab' in GitHub via org admin.
- Launched full scan of jmp-priv-us-east file system for persistence artifacts.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-13 09:15 UTC - Security alert triage queue: Bastion anomaly fired (threshold: new interactive session + unusual geo).
09:20 - Reached out to employee (Sarah O'Hara) who confirmed she clicked a LinkedIn message and completed a consent-like flow; she denies approving MFA push.
09:25 - Correlated OAuth grant: external app 'ExternalCollab' obtained a GitHub authorization token at 09:07 from IP 18.205.33.12; likely step-down to access internal helper via web callback.
09:35 - SRE snapshot of jump host shows /tmp/tmpX3 and a one-line token; no persistence binaries found, but .ssh/authorized_keys modified at 09:10 (new key added: SSH-RSA AAAA...).

09:50 - Hypothesis 1: user was social-engineered into granting an OAuth token that was then used to retrieve stored credentials or run a remote action that executed token-fetcher on their workstation which in turn performed the SSH.
10:10 - Hypothesis 2: credential replay using harvested SSH private key combined with session hijack; less likely given MFA prompt observed.
11:25 - Evidence points to an automated chain: LinkedIn message -> OAuth consent page -> GitHub token -> remote exec/payload -> SSH from foreign IP with short-lived token.
comments: Aisha Patel (Security): Notified on-call SRE and blocked the source IP. Prioritize token rotation and user session invalidation.
Priya Kapoor (SRE): Confirmed removal of added authorized_key and restored from snapshot. Collected memory and /tmp artifacts for forensic imaging.

Mateo Ruiz (Incident Response): Recommend issuing org-wide warning about malicious LinkedIn invites and initiating phishing hash scan across employee inboxes. Need CISO sign-off for external notification if lateral access confirmed.

Sarah O'Hara (Employee): I clicked one message that looked like a shared doc; it asked me to allow access to GitHub. I thought it was legit because it showed 'Redwood' in the URL. I did not approve any MFA prompts.
Liam Chen (Assignee): Gathering IAM logs and will enumerate all AssumeRole events in the last 24 hours; starting privilege account rotations and will coordinate with SecOps for containment checklist.
recommended_next_steps: 1) Full rotate of any keys/tokens used by infra-maintainer and any STS sessions issued in the window. 2) Forensic analysis of employee workstation and jump host snapshots (for secure archive). 3) Phishing outreach: contact impacted employee cohort with indicators and guidance. 4) Update Bastion rules to require re-approval for suspicious geo or device changes. 5) Run an org-wide scan for similar OAuth grants and unusual app installations.
resolution: Containment in progress as of 2026-03-14: blocked offending IPs, rotated implicated tokens, revoked OAuth app authorization, removed malicious SSH key, and forced affected user password reset. Forensics collected for both workstation and jump host. Pending items: (a) confirm whether any data exfiltration occurred (SRE to complete log aggregation), (b) complete organization-wide scan for grants and remediate. Incident remains open until log review completes and CISO sign-off for closure.
post_incident_actions:
- Create new runbook entry: 'LinkedIn-OAuth-Chain-Phish' with detection playbooks.
- Add automated detection rule to flag new OAuth grants for external apps with repo or write scopes.
- Implement stricter Bastion policies: deny interactive sudo from foreign IPs without prior allowlist.
- Schedule company phishing awareness and simulated test for Q2.
